newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols rebound as spot touches 118.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols rebound as spot touches 118.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen options bounced off early lows as the greenback leapt to 118 yen in U.S. trading, dealers said.
Shorter-dated volatilities, which had been nearly half a point lower from Wednesday in European hours, were bid back up in hectic spot-driven activity, they said.
"The front end is really spot-sensitive," said a U.S. bank dealer in Chicago.
One-month dollar/yen implied volatility jumped to 11.2/11.5 percent by the U.S. early afternoon from lows near 10.6/10.8 earlier and 11.0/11.3 at Wednesday's close.

Still, the dollar/yen volatility curve, which had been gradually steepening its positive slope this week, did not flatten as the back months were also lifted by a big one-year purchase totaling some $200-300 million in notional value.
That single buyer bid up one-year volatility by a quarter point from early levels to about 12.1 percent, an interbank broker in New York noted. One-year on Wednesday finished at 11.4/11.7 percent.
"As a result, a lot of people (who took the other side of the trade) were spreading out of it to six-month or three-month, so they also got a little bid," the broker added.
"It's been a really thin market and people do run away very quickly," the broker said. "Two hundred (million dollars) was really enough to shift the curve."

The dollar jumped toward 118 yen in mid-morning after grinding slowly higher to the mid-116.50 area overnight. Lingering concerns over Asian currencies weighed on the yen against the dollar as well as on the crosses.

Kyoko Hiramatsu, a senior dealer at Bank of Yokohama, said the 200-day moving average, which has been the dividing range for the dollar/yen market's sentiment recently, came in at around 118.20 yen and capped today's rally.
"Once we're above the 200-day moving average, I think volatilities would start picking up again," she said.

She said the dollar/yen curve had steepened enough to warrant some flattening should the dollar remain unstable and threaten the boundaries of the recent 114-120 yen range, but added that the current level seemed not quite critical enough.
Traders said the market would likely remain cautious ahead of next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
The rally away from 115 yen was tipping the scale toward the dollar's upside risks, and risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, were moving toward yen puts.

One-month 25-delta risk reversal was assessed at around par at U.S. midsession after trading slightly in favor of yen calls since late last week. The very short maturities briefly flipped for yen puts after today's spot rally.
Dollar/mark volatilities were mostly steady as the dollar looked consolidative, trading largely between 1.8350 and 1.8450 marks.
The whole curve from one-month to one-year was assessed at about 11.0/11.2 percent, roughly unchanged from Wednesday.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal stayed marginally skewed for mark puts.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
